text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament will vote on Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) cabinet and its programme.
-- Deputies from the Union of National Salvation (UNS), which includes ethnic Turks and monarchists, would vote for the UDF cabinet, a senior UNS official said.

-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party, whose cabinet stepped down in February after month-long street protests, said it has recommended to its deputies in the new parliament to vote against the UDF cabinet and its programme.
-- Bulgaria has to speed up crucial reforms in its armed forces to support its bid for a NATO membership, President Petar Stoyanov said.

-- A visiting International Monetary Fund mission urged Bulgaria's Finance ministry to assume lower wages than previously anticipated in the country's industrial and public sector under a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency supervisory board elected Assen Dyulgerov as its chairman.

-- Some two billion dollars were expected to be invested in Bulgaria's transport sector by the year 2000, said interim transport minister Wilhelm Kraus, who would keep his post in the new UDF cabinet.

-- Some 590 Bulgarian firms of a total of 1,050 listed for voucher privatisation are majority private-owned following the second tender of the country's mass sell-off programme in April, head of the Mass Privatisation Centre Pirin Atanasov said.
-- Bulgaria's Bank for Agricultural Credit was in talks with a potential foreign buyer expected to invest $20 million in the ailing bank and help it avoid bankruptcy.
